stories.title: US AI data-center backlash: OpenAI weighs rebranding them "AI compute campuses" as the industry courts kids with field trips
stories.summary:
Public backlash against AI data centers over power costs, water use, and land is reshaping where and how projects get built, and is forcing Big Tech into both concessions and new persuasion campaigns.

- New: OpenAI might rebrand its data centers as "AI compute campuses" to dodge their unpopularity, TechCrunch reports, in a push tied to policy chief Chris Lehane
- Industry-friendly groups are courting young people with data center field trips and other youth outreach, per Wired
- Amazon pledged to stop using NDAs with local governments, paired with a warning to critics not to get in the way
- Nearly $200 billion worth of US projects have been blocked or delayed this year; Trump admitted in a Time interview that he is a NIMBY on data centers
- Big Tech is countering with a multimillion-dollar ad campaign and a "viral" pro-data-center party backed by Peter Thiel and the Koch Institute
- Environmental-justice concerns in previously industrialized neighborhoods remain a central line of attack

stories.title: OpenAI reportedly lowers the target for its pre-IPO raise, last pegged at $30B and a $1.25T valuation
stories.summary:
OpenAI's last planned private raise before a public debut is reportedly falling short of expectations, and the company has lowered its funding target.

- The round was last reported at $30 billion and a $1.25 trillion valuation, already down from the $1.4 trillion figure reported in late September

- It's expected to be OpenAI's final private raise before an IPO, now pushed to 2027
- Altman has said OpenAI must "be able to make confident safety claims" before going public, tying the IPO to getting its rogue-AI incidents under control, per Gizmodo

stories.title: Anthropic officially files for its IPO, with a public S-1 showing soaring revenue, heavy losses, and founder control

Anthropic has officially filed for its public debut, making its S-1 public after weeks of leaks, investor objections to its financials, and political calls for delay.

- The filing shows soaring revenue and major enterprise adoption alongside mounting losses; Engadget earlier put last year's net loss at about $8 billion
- Anthropic may be valued as high as $2 trillion, with a stock market debut reportedly planned for November
- Its seven co-founders get a combined 50.1% of the vote on most matters, meant to preserve founder control and its safety mission
- Note conversions show Amazon is set to make far more from the IPO than Anthropic's VC backers, and the SpaceXAI deal is bigger than previously known
- Risk factors include a warning that Anthropic's own AI could pose an existential risk to humanity
- New: Blackstone forecasts that credit agencies will give Anthropic a high "junk" rating after the IPO, which would make funding its massive spending harder and costlier, per the FT

stories.summary:
Nvidia released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, a free multilingual speech-to-text model, alongside Granary v2, announced on the Hugging Face blog.

- Transcribes up to 40 languages and, per Nvidia, can be prompted and adapted
- Works only on recorded audio, not live streams, per TechCrunch
- Positioned as a big step for meeting and medical transcription tools, while real-time use stays with rivals like ElevenLabs

sources.title: Voice AI in vogue: Nvidia releases new open transcription model
NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and Granary v2: Intelligent Multilingual Transcription You Can Prompt and Adapt
